Appended.description: The records took seqs `first_seq` to `next_seq` (exclusive), at `time`. A replay (`replayed`) of an earlier attempt with the same idempotency key reports that attempt's records.

Consumer.description: A consumer's cursor: the seq it reads from next, and how many records it has yet to read.

CreateApiKey.description: `rate_limit`: requests per second this key may make on each node (default: the node's per-key limit).

CreateStream.description: Names are 1-128 characters of `[A-Za-z0-9_.:-]`. Records older than `retention_ms`, or beyond the newest `max_bytes`, may be trimmed; trims run once a stream is a sixteenth past a limit, and take it back to the limit.

DbInfo.description: `role` is what you may do here: readers read, writers also write, admins also delete the database.

DbStats.description: The database at the version read (at most 5 s stale). `levels` lists segments by level, shallowest first; `size_bytes` (blobs included) counts against `quota_bytes`.

DbSummary.description: `org` is the owning organization (null for your own databases).

DeleteRows.description: Exactly one of `pk` (one row; answers `found`) or `where` (every row it selects, at most `limit`; answers `count`).

Filter.description: A row filter: `and`, `or` or `not` of filters, or a comparison of the column `col`. A missing or null operand fails every comparison, `ne` included; `exists` tests for one. Numbers compare by value.

value.description: Absent for `exists`, an array of at most 1000 for `in`, otherwise not null.

Headers.description: Header names (1-128 bytes) to values (at most 4 KiB); at most 64.

IndexInfo.description: A `building` index is maintained by writes but cannot be queried until its backfill finishes.

KvChange.description: A key's value as of the feed's snapshot (with `expires_at` if it expires), a key deleted (`deleted`, also once its value expired), or every key in `[start, end)` deleted (`deleted_range`; `end: null` is the end of the keyspace).

KvItem.description: A key and its value. Keys/values that are not valid UTF-8 in utf8 mode are returned in `key_b64` / `value_b64`. Values stored as blobs larger than the inline JSON limit only carry `blob`. A value written with a time to live has `expires_at` (cluster time, ms), unless the transaction reading it wrote it itself.

NewRecord.description: Exactly one of `value` (a string in the request's encoding) and `json` (any JSON value). A record takes at most 1 MiB.

Op.description: One operation. Keys and values are UTF-8 strings unless the request sets `encoding: base64`. `ttl_ms` makes a value or row expire that long after the write commits; an update keeps a row's expiry unless it sets one. `update_rows` and `delete_rows` change every row `where` selects (at most `limit`), all within the transaction's write limit, and return `count`. Stream ops: `append` gets its seqs at commit (`expect_seq` fails the transaction with 412 unless the stream's next seq is still that); `read_stream` conflicts with appends only if it reached the stream's end, and sees the transaction's own trims but not its appends; `stream_info` conflicts with every append; `set_consumer` takes a seq at most the stream's next.

OpResult.description: Result of one op; the fields present depend on the op (see Op). An `append` reports `first_seq` once the transaction commits.

PasswordChange.description: `current_password` is required for accounts that have a password.

Query.description: Scan the primary key (default) or a secondary index: equality on a prefix of its columns (`eq`), an optional range on the next column, a residual filter, and pagination via `cursor`.

Row.description: Column name to value. `bytes` are base64; `blob` columns take a staged `blob_id` on write and return BlobMeta on read.

RowChange.description: A row as of the feed's snapshot, or its primary key and `deleted`.

Selection.description: Rows to change, selected like a query: the primary key or an index (`index`), equality on a prefix of its columns (`eq`), a range on the next column and a residual filter. `{}` selects every row.

SessionInfo.description: A signed-in session: `client` is the address that signed in, `current` the session making the request.

SetConsumer.description: At most the stream's next seq.

Stream.description: Records `first_seq` to `next_seq` (exclusive) are kept: `bytes` of bodies and headers, appended from `first_time` to `last_time`. Stream info lists the first 100 consumers; `consumers_next_cursor` continues the listing on the consumers route.

StreamConfig.description: Fields left out keep their value; `null` removes a limit.

StreamFilter.description: A record filter: `and`, `or` or `not` of filters, or a comparison of a JSON body `field` (a dotted path; numeric segments index arrays), a `header`, or, naming neither, the body's text, which only `contains` tests. A missing or null operand fails every comparison, `ne` included; `exists` tests for one. Numbers compare by value.

value.description: Absent for `exists`, an array of at most 1000 for `in`, otherwise not null.
Absent for `exists`, an array of at most 1000 for `in`, otherwise not null.

StreamRead.description: Records from at most one of `from_seq`, `from_time` (the first record at or after it), `tail` (the last N) and `consumer` (its cursor; a new consumer starts at the beginning), up to `until_seq` or `until_time` (exclusive), oldest first or with `reverse` newest first; at most `limit` (default 100) records and about `max_bytes` (default 4 MiB, at most 16 MiB). With `filter`, at most `scan_limit` records (default 10,000) are examined.

StreamRecord.description: `seq` is the record's position; `time` (cluster time, ms) is when its append committed. Its body is `json`, or `value` (`value_b64` if not UTF-8 in utf8 mode).

StreamRecords.description: `next_seq` continues the read: the next `from_seq` of a forward read, the next `until_seq` of a reverse one. `done`: the read reached its end. `first_seq` and `tail_seq` are the stream's first and next seqs.

TxnResult.description: `appends`: the first seq each append received, in order.

UpdateRows.description: Exactly one of `pk` (one row; answers `found`) or `where` (every row it selects, at most `limit`; answers `count`). A row keeps its expiry unless `ttl_ms` sets one.

info.description: Transactional key-value, table and stream databases on object storage. Authenticate with `Authorization: Bearer <session token or API key>` (or the `brs_session` cookie). Errors use the Error schema with a stable `code`; `retryable` errors may be retried (use idempotency keys for writes). Requests over a rate limit get 429 `rate_limited` with `Retry-After` and were not applied; writes that would take a database past its size quota get 507 `quota_exceeded`. Every response carries an `x-request-id` header: the client's own (1-64 characters of `[A-Za-z0-9._:-]`) or a new one, which the server's logs record on every node the request reaches.

get.description: As JSON, a page of records. As NDJSON, a record per line, with the page's `next_seq`, `first_seq`, `tail_seq` and `done` in `x-baserunna-*` headers. As server-sent events (forward reads only), each record as `id: <seq>` and `data: <record>`, then each later append for up to `wait_ms`, with a comment every 15 s while idle; the stream ends at `limit` records, at `until_seq` or `until_time`, after `wait_ms`, or when the node shuts down, and resumes after `Last-Event-ID`. A read that fails before its first record answers with an error status.
